# Review, iliad-138 (22.1–89), units.json

Two passes. Pass 1: every grammatical label, position claim and cross-reference in the notes, checked against the Greek line and the published English (Book 20 and 21 parts, iliad-130/131/132/133/137). Pass 2: Greek → `l`, `l` ↔ `i`, remembered English, quotation marks and `mark`/`p` flags, and every `l`/`i` against the house-renderings table (both conventions files). `t` was not touched (verified identical to the draft). Scansion flags: none, nothing to add.

Severity: **high** = a false statement (grammar, fact, cross-reference) that would ship; **medium** = departs from the house table or from the sense; **low** = unsupported or loose wording, softened.

Structure checked and fine: line division of `l` equals `t` in all 47 units; paragraph flags `p` fall on lines 1, 14, 21, 25, 38, 77 only; each speech has `mark` on its first unit (Apollo 8, Achilles 15, Priam 38, Hecuba 82) and “ / ” in both `l` and `i` on first and last units (13, 20, 76, 89). 22.14 and 22.32 are identical to iliad-099 and iliad-079 in `l` and `i`. Speeches begin and end inside this part, so no neighbouring-part check was needed; the end of iliad-137 (21.611) closes no speech.

## The three claims the drafter flagged

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| (a) 22.27–29 star = Sirius | The poem says only “the dog of Orion”. Sirius is the standard identification but not stated by the text. Softened (unit 15). |
| (b) 22.79–80 mother = Hecuba | Not named in 22.1–89. Hecuba is Hector’s mother (already stated in the note to iliad-038), so the identification is sound, but the note now says she is not named here (unit 41). |
| (c) 22.46–48 / 22.51 and Book 21 | **Verified.** iliad-132 (21.84–85): Lycaon says his mother Laothoe was “the daughter of old Altes”, and (21.89) that she bore two sons to Priam. iliad-130/131 (20.407–419) Polydorus is killed; iliad-133 (21.114ff.) Lycaon is killed. So Priam’s ignorance of both deaths at 22.46–48 and the note “the reader has seen Polydorus die in Book 20 and Lycaon in Book 21” are true. The one loose claim was “Laothoe is a daughter of Altes (51)”: line 51 says only παιδί, and the parentage comes from Book 21. Now cited to 21.84–85 (units 26, 28). The note’s statement that Apollo has been luring Achilles in disguise is also true (iliad-137, 21.599–604, as Agenor). |

## Considered and refused

- ἀκέοντο `i` “eased” vs table ἀκέομαι `l` “heal” / `i` “cure”, “mend” (4.36, 13.115): declared in new-renderings.md (“quenched”, “slaked” avoided on purpose); “cure” would fit the table but “eased” is a defensible choice for a thirst and is not wrong. Left.
- ἐπέσχον (83) and ἀνέσχε (80) both `l` “held out”: different verbs, but the second recalls the first gesture, and “held out” is right for both. Left.
- Unit 29 `l` “houses” vs `i` “house” of Hades: idiomatic singular in English, plural kept in the literal layer. Left.
- ὀλοώτατε “most baneful”: the table’s only superlative-type row (3.365 “deadlier”) is Odyssey wording for a different word form; ὀλοός is “baneful/baleful” elsewhere. Left.
- νωμάω “plied” (23) vs table 10.358 “set moving” / note “ply”: the table note itself gives “ply”. Left.
- “bitten the earth” (9): not a remembered English phrase; it follows the table’s ὀδὰξ … γαῖαν “bite the earth” (2.418). Left.
- “a queen among women” (48): new-renderings.md; “queen” is a gloss on κρείουσα but defensible and declared. Left.
- Andromache named in the note to 88 (the wife): not in these lines, but Hector’s wife is established earlier in the poem, and the note says “the wife”. Left.
- The `about` text (“from the wall begs Hector”): Priam’s position on the wall is clear from 38–60; left.

## Gloss pass

All 95 novel entries and 20 broadened entries checked against the lines and units.json `l`/`i`; format checks (typographic ’ only, under 230 characters, no line numbers, no “here”, broadened = old entry whole + ' · ' + new) all pass. 12 edits:

- αἰσχύνωσι: “disgrace, dishonour, defile;” → “disgrace, dishonour, disfigure, defile;”
- δαμασθείς: “(= ἐδαμάσθην)” → “(aor. pass. ἐδαμάσθην, ἐδάμην)”
- θάλος: “young shoot, sapling; of a child, ’a sprig’” → “young shoot, sapling; of a child, ’a scion’”
- λαθικηδέα: “soothing sorrow, banishing care;” → “soothing sorrow, banishing care, making one forget cares;”
- σευάμενος: “aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg., epic unaugmented stem:” → “aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg., from the epic aor. (ἐσσευάμην, σεύατο):”
- ἐπάλξεσιν: “fem. dat. pl., epic -εσιν (= Attic ἐπάλξεσι), after” → “fem. dat. pl., after”
- ἔβλαψάς: “’you have thwarted’” → “’you have harmed’”
- ὀρέξῃς: “in a prohibition after μή: ’do not grant’” → “in a negative purpose clause continuing ὄφρα, after μή: ’(that you) not offer’”
- αἴσῃ: “fem. dat. sg., after ἐν: ’in a grievous lot’ (ἐν ἀργαλέῃ αἴσῃ)” → “fem. dat. sg., of means with ἐν: ’by a grievous lot’ (ἐν ἀργαλέῃ αἴσῃ)”
- μενεαίνεις: “absolute: ’you rage’ (ἀσπερχὲς μενεαίνεις ’you rage unceasingly’)” → “absolute, no infinitive: ’you are eager’ (ἀσπερχὲς μενεαίνεις ’you are eager without pause’)”
- προτὶ: “’against, on’” → “’to, against’”
- ἔλθοι: “’would come’ (ἄχος ἔλθοι ’grief would come’)” → “’would come, would go’ (ἀπὸ πραπίδων ἄχος ἔλθοι ’grief would go from the heart’)”

Reasons: αἰσχύνωσι, λαθικηδέα, θάλος, ἔβλαψάς, μενεαίνεις, προτὶ, ἔλθοι: meaning lists and quoted renderings brought into agreement with `l`/`i` (disfigure; forget cares; scion; harmed; eager; to the ground; go from the heart). ὀρέξῃς: parse was wrong (negative purpose continuing ὄφρα, not a prohibition). δαμασθείς: "(= ἐδαμάσθην)" was misleading for a participle. σευάμενος: "unaugmented" is meaningless for a participle. ἐπάλξεσιν: -εσιν is not specifically epic. αἴσῃ: ἐν + dat. is of means, matching `i` "by a grievous fate".

Considered and refused: κλαύσομαι "(= Attic κλαύσομαι)" (same form, harmless); ἐρύουσιν as pres. with ἄν/κε, futurate (a short-vowel subj. is possible but the entry's rendering is right); ἄρηϊ "dat. of means" (acceptable beside ’in war’); εὖνιν, ἐπιδόντα, κταμένῳ, ἄλεν and all other parses verified correct.
